claims.text: a type DECLARED IN F, matched on its full in-file qualname (so Outer.Inner resolves and a bare Inner does not -- searching nested qualnames by leaf name is exactly the fabrication I5 forbids);
claims.why: Resolution logic not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Module-name -> file resolution is done by FILTERING the import edges index.py already computed, never by re-resolving imports here, so a type edge can never contradict the import graph: if the import edge is absent, so is the type edge.
claims.why: Refers to index.py and resolution logic not in this chunk.

claims.text: A STAR IMPORT IS NOT A TIER. from m import * is walked, but only to DETECT an ambiguity -- it can never be the single winner, because what a star actually binds depends on m.__all__ (a bare assignment, which parse.py does not record) and on the leading-underscore rule, and because a star from a module outside this repo can supply the same name unseen.
claims.why: Refers to _star_candidates function not present in this chunk.

claims.why: Refers to a test file not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Builtins (str, int, Exception) and typing vocabulary (Protocol, Literal) are counted in their own buckets rather than as failures, because folding them into unresolved would make the coverage number a lie in one direction (1722 mentions of str in daedalus/ are not 1722 gaps).
claims.why: Classification logic not shown in this chunk; constants _VOCABULARY and _BUILTIN_TYPES are defined but usage not shown.

claims.text: A name bound by an import whose module is NOT in this repo is external, not unresolved: 'declared somewhere else' and 'declared nowhere' are different facts and a report that merges them cannot be acted on.
claims.why: Classification logic not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: Every iteration that can reach output is over a sorted sequence, every published list is sorted by a total order, and no counter is derived from a set's iteration order.
claims.why: Iteration and sorting not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: union_id comes from parse.union_id (derived from the site's identity, never from a counter) for the same reason.
claims.why: Import of union_id from .parse is present on line 96.

claims.text: Bump when the MEANING of a published node, edge or coverage key changes. Separate from TYPE_FACTS_VERSION (the EXTRACTOR's version) because the two move independently: a resolution fix does not change what was extracted, and a reader has to be able to tell which half produced a number.
claims.why: TYPE_GRAPH_VERSION = "1" is defined; TYPE_FACTS_VERSION is imported from .parse but its value is not shown; the claim about separation is a directive, not a checkable fact.

claims.text: RELATIONS tuple contains exactly the six relations.
claims.why: RELATIONS is defined as a tuple of six strings: REL_HAS_FIELD, REL_FIELD_TYPE, REL_INHERITS, REL_CONSUMES, REL_PRODUCES, REL_ALIAS_OF.

claims.text: _CAPPED_RELATIONS = frozenset({REL_CONSUMES, REL_PRODUCES})
claims.why: Constant _CAPPED_RELATIONS is defined as frozenset with exactly those two relations.

claims.text: MEASURED on daedalus/ (143 files, 2207 functions, 2182 carrying >=1 type edge, 227 distinct nominal types) BEFORE this module existed
claims.why: Measurement data is comment, not code; cannot verify.

claims.text: 0 disables it.
claims.why: Refers to behavior of hub cap when set to 0; not implemented in this chunk.

claims.text: A protocol with a single common member name (run, close) matches half a repo by coincidence, which is the fixture corpus's own argument (emit/flush 'make coincidence the normal case'), so one member is not evidence. And a protocol that matches more classes than the cap has told us nothing at all: the whole match set is dropped rather than truncated, because publishing the first N of an arbitrary set is a guess wearing a number.
claims.why: Refers to structural matching logic not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Field origins in preference order when the same member was written twice -- limit: int = 10 in the class body AND self.limit = limit in __init__ are two facts about ONE member (parse.py says so explicitly), and two field nodes for one member would be a fabrication. An ANNOTATED origin always wins first; this order only breaks the remaining ties.
claims.why: _ORIGIN_RANK is defined with keys 'annassign', 'self', 'assign', 'enum_member' in that order, matching the described preference.

claims.text: Typing / ABC vocabulary that is a WORD IN THE LANGUAGE, not a repo type. Counted in its own bucket so it never inflates unresolved. Most of these arrive with an explicit from typing import ... and are classified external before this set is consulted; the set catches the spellings that arrive with no binding at all. A repo that genuinely DECLARES one of these names shadows it, because tier 1 (same-file declaration) runs first.
claims.why: Usage of _VOCABULARY not shown in this chunk; classification logic absent.

claims.text: Names bound in every module by the interpreter itself. Asked of builtins rather than hand-listed so the set cannot drift from the interpreter running the scan, and filtered to actual TYPES so that len/print (never legal in an annotation) are not silently treated as resolved-away vocabulary. Every exception class comes along for free, which matters: -> ValueError is a real annotation shape and it is not an unresolved repo type.
claims.why: _BUILTIN_TYPES is defined using vars(builtins) and filtered to types, with None and NoneType added.

claims.text: Forest node id for a type declaration.
claims.why: type_node_id returns f"type:{module}#{qualname}".

claims.text: Forest node id for one member of a type.
claims.why: field_node_id returns f"field:{module}#{qualname}.{field_name}".

claims.text: Deliberately NOT a forest node id: functions are not forest nodes today (the forest's nodes are files and documents), so consumes/produces attach to the FILE node and carry this string in their attributes.
claims.why: function_ref returns f"{module}#{qualname}" without type: or field: prefix.

claims.text: True for a type/field node id. For forest and dss guards.
claims.why: is_type_node_id returns True if node_id starts with 'type:' or 'field:'.

claims.text: The repo-root dotted namespace, for callers that have no _PyNaming. index.build_index passes its own _PyNaming (the authority: it knows about declared package roots and center-relative spellings). This is the no-center view, which is what an unconfigured repo gets anyway, and it exists so tools and tests can resolve without importing index -- which they must not do, because index imports THIS module.
